Points, lines, areas, segments and text

Source: R/layers.R
og_point.Rd

A layer of a map, one mark for each row of the data. og_point() draws a circle at each row's position (pings, stations, catches); og_line() draws rows that are lines (tows, transects, cables); og_segment() draws a line from each row's start to its end (a tow from shooting to hauling); og_polygon() draws areas, filled and outlined; og_text() writes a column's values at the rows' positions (place names, station ids). Each is piped onto a map, og_map(data) |> og_point(colour = speed), or given the data first, data |> og_point(), which starts a map. The data stay in DuckDB and reach the page as vector tiles, so a map of millions of rows stays fast and its colours change in the page.

  popup = TRUE,
  labels = NULL,
  codes = NULL,
  hover = NULL,
  choose = NULL,
  search = NULL,

  id = NULL,
  info = NULL,
  section = "Layers",

Arguments

map

An og_map(), or the data, which start a map.

data

The rows, if not the map's: a parquet file, folder or glob, a lazy DuckDB table, a data frame or an sf object (points, or lines and areas for og_line() and og_polygon(); a table's shapes in a column geometry as DuckDB's GEOMETRY or WKB).

lon, lat

The position's columns, by default lon and lat; for og_segment() its start.

colour

The marks' colour (an area's outline): a colour ("#c0392b"), or a column written bare (colour = speed), coloured by palette; several columns, c(behaviour, speed), are a choice in the page, the first shown. A column's colours by default: Okabe-Ito for up to eight values, Paired for up to twelve, Glasbey's 32 beyond, the rest grey as "other"; viridis for an ordered factor and for numbers, dates and times. color is the same.

size

A point's diameter, a text's size (a number, or for text a column written bare), in pixels. For points, by default, a size that follows the zoom: the least, 2 pixels, until the zoom at which most points lie that far apart, then doubling with each zoom in, as a size on the ground does, up to the most, 8; size = c(1, 12) gives other bounds, one number a size that stays.

stroke

For og_point(), a ring: its width in pixels. Each point is drawn as a ring of its colour, hollow, size the diameter inside it; a click on it or inside it shows the row.

opacity

The marks' opacity, 0-1.

whole

How the rows reach the page: TRUE, whole, as one GeoJSON file read once (no further fetching as the reader zooms and pans, nothing cut at a tile's edge, one file in a bundle); FALSE, as vector tiles cut by DuckDB as the page asks for them, which keep a page light however many rows there are. By default (NULL) whole when its GeoJSON is at most 5 MB (some 30,000 points; a table of more than 50,000 rows is not tried), else as tiles: measured on layers of real data, the two are equal in a browser up to about 5 MB, and a whole layer needs nothing more of R once read, so a served map pans and zooms while R is busy. Above it a whole layer is slower and heavier (about 50 MB of a browser's memory for each MB of GeoJSON).

thin

For points: in each tile, one point for each screen pixel, TRUE (each colour, each value a choose list picks and each group of a time panel keeping its own), so a tile of millions of rows reaches the page as what can be seen of them; a number of pixels for coarser cells; FALSE keeps every point. At the layer's deepest zoom (maxzoom, 14 by default) and beyond, only points that would be drawn on one spot are dropped.

palette

The colours for a column, in place of the default: a palette's name (from og_palettes(), palette.pals() or hcl.pals(), written loosely: "set1" is Set 1), colours, colours named by value (c(Fishing = "#c0392b")), or a function of n (viridisLite::mako).

limits, stretch

For a numeric column: the values the palette's ends stand at (by default its 1st and 99th percentile), and how the colours spread between them, "linear", "log" or "equal" (equal shares of the values).

legend

Whether the layer has a legend.

popup

The columns a click shows, written bare, or a variable holding their names; TRUE, every column; FALSE, no popup. A click shows the row as a table, read from the server (a bundle carries the rows): a column's name, its unit beside it and its description behind it, where the data's dictionary or labels give them.

labels

The columns' names as the popup shows them, in place of the data's: c(speed = "Speed (knots)"). By default a data frame's column attributes (label, units) or a parquet file's own dictionary (an entry of data-dict.tidyverse.org's format in its metadata, as og_example()'s files hold), else the column's name.

codes

The labels of a coded column's values, shown beside each code: a named list by column, each a named vector (c("6" = "bottom trawl")) or a table of code and label; by default the dictionary's, where it has them.

hover

A column whose value is shown beside the pointer.

choose

The columns, written bare, whose values the reader picks to show of this layer alone, each under the layer's name: text, a factor, a logical or a whole number (an id, a code) as a list (chips for up to 12 values, else a list to show one at a time), a fraction, a date or a time as a range with two handles, unless the data's dictionary declares otherwise (as for og_map()); ‹ and › step through either. Several are linked: each offers only the values the others leave. For choices that drive every layer with the column, give choose to og_map().

search

A column written bare (search = name), its values as text, for the page's Find box: whole matches first, then values it begins, then any holding it, case and accents aside, each kind nearest the view's centre first, with their count; a click on one takes the map there, at zoom 10 or nearer (a text's own start zoom where it has one), turns its layer on and shows its row. The column's texts and places go to the page on its first search (a bundle carries them); a layer of more than 500,000 rows takes none.

name, id, info

The layer's name in the sidebar, its id, and the text behind its ⓘ. The id (lower-case letters, digits and _) is the key the page's address and a page's own script know the layer by, its styles <id>-dot, <id>-line, <id>-fill and <id>-text; by default made from the name.

section

The sidebar's box the layer sits in, by its title. The layer is drawn over those added before it, whatever their boxes, unless og_map()'s order says otherwise.

visible

Whether the layer is on when the page opens.

minzoom, maxzoom

The zoom the layer is drawn from, and its tiles' deepest (14 by default), past which the map draws that zoom's tiles larger. For og_text(), minzoom may be a column written bare: each row from its own zoom, from the first whole zoom at or above it (MapLibre judges a zoom in a filter at whole zooms), so a text due at 7.4 shows from 8.

...

MapLibre's own paint and layout properties for the layer's styles, by MapLibre's names in quotes: "circle-stroke-color" = "white" (a ring of another colour round a filled point), "line-dasharray" = list(2, 1), "text-halo-width" = 0. Each goes to the styles of its kind (circle, line, fill; text, icon and symbol on a text's), as paint or layout as MapLibre has it; an expression is a list, list("get", "size"). color is taken for colour.

linewidth

A line's width (an area's outline), in pixels.

lon_end, lat_end

For og_segment(), the columns of its end.

fill

For og_polygon(), the areas' colour, as colour is for the other marks; NA, none: the outline alone, in colour, 2 pixels wide unless linewidth says otherwise, a click inside an area still showing its row.

label

For og_text(), the column whose values are written, bare. On a line (data whose shapes are lines), the text is written along it, at its middle.

angle, priority, fontface, offset, overlap

For og_text(), each a value or a column written bare: angle, the text turned that many degrees counter-clockwise, as ggplot2's; priority, which text is placed first where two would meet, the higher (within a tile, as MapLibre places); fontface, "plain", "italic", "bold" or "bold.italic", in the base map's own fonts for that face; offset, c(x, y) in text heights, x to the right and y up (a column takes at most 256 pairs of values); overlap, TRUE to draw every text where others meet (MapLibre leaves out the later). A turned text keeps the upright box round it clear of others.

Value

An og_map() with the layer added.

See also

og_map(); og_layer() for a layer in MapLibre's own terms.

Examples

# \donttest{
m <- og_example("dansk") |>
  og_point(colour = c(behaviour, speed), popup = c(vessel_id, time_stamp, speed))
format(m)
#> [1] "<og_map> Map"              "  layers: points (vector)"
og_map(og_example("trawlsurveytows")) |> og_line(name = "Tows") |> format()
#> [1] "<og_map> Map"             "  layers: tows (geojson)"
og_example("dansk_harbours") |> og_polygon(fill = "#d9822b", popup = SI_HARB) |> format()
#> [1] "<og_map> Map"              "  layers: areas (geojson)"
# }
